To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the processing of emotional faces is not automatic and that the neural processing and representation of emotional stimuli is under the same attentional control as other stimulus categories.
the processing of emotional stimuli, similar to that of other stimulus categories is under top-down attentional control.
the competition among multiple stimuli in the visual scene is biased by attention and that emotional stimuli, like other stimuli, require attentional processing resources to activate the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that underlie the processing of emotional stimuli in the human brain.
the mechanisms that allow us to select and process relevant information in the presence of a large amount of irrelevant or distracting information.
the mechanisms that control the competition among multiple stimuli for neural representation, and the results reveal the importance of top-down control in the processing of emotional stimuli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
attentional modulation of visual processing is not limited to the processing of nonemotional information but extends to the processing of emotional information as well.

the processing of stimuli with high emotional content is not "automatically" processed, and instead, the processing of emotional stimuli requires attention, but it is not clear whether the attentional resources are allocated by a top-down or bottom-up process.
attentional control of neural and emotional processing is a function of the amount of attentional resources available for processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

attentional control of the neural processing of emotional stimuli is a general phenomenon, and the processing of emotional stimuli, like that of other stimulus categories is under top-down biasing control.
the neural processing is not automatic and requires some attentional resources.
the processing of emotional faces is not automatic and that the amygdala is not an exception.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processing of emotional stimuli is not automatic but requires the deployment of attentional resources.
attentional resources are required for processing emotional stimuli and that the neural processing is not automatic, contrary to prevailing views.
attentional control of the neural processing of emotional stimuli is not automatic but requires attentional engagement.
